chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) wore al-Taq (a cap), and al-Saj (a cloak), and al-Khamais (striped woolen garments).

key_terms.السَّاجُ: Al-Saj — a large outer cloak or pallium, typically of Yemeni or Persian origin, often used as a mantle
key_terms.الطَّاقُ: Al-Taq — a type of cap or woven head covering, historically worn in the Arabian Peninsula
key_terms.الْخَمَائِصُ: Al-Khamais (sing. khamisa) — a black striped woolen garment, a well-known type of outer robe in early Islamic dress

ai.seo_question: What types of clothing did the Prophet Muhammad wear according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) wore three types of garments: al-Taq (a type of cap or head covering), al-Saj (a pallium or draped outer cloak), and al-Khamais (striped woolen robes). This hadith belongs to the chapter on dress (al-libas) in al-Kafi and establishes Prophetic precedent for wearing these specific types of clothing. Early Muslim communities looked to such narrations to determine what forms of dress were consistent with Prophetic sunnah, particularly regarding textiles and styles appropriate for men.
